fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. The text says Josiah "…walked in all the ways of his father David…" (2 Kings 22:2). David is the king Israel anointed at Hebron (2 Samuel 5:3). So the man on the throne at eight years old is following a path that was already marked out for him.

Saul was a king of Israel (1 Samuel 11:15), so I see why he came to mind. But he isn't the name in the text. Verse 2 says Josiah "…walked in all the ways of his father David…" David is the one Josiah follows. Keep your eye on that name, friend.

Jeroboam was made king over all Israel (1 Kings 12:20), but the text doesn't send Josiah down his road. It says Josiah "…walked in all the ways of his father David…" (2 Kings 22:2). David's the name on this one, friend. Jeroboam can sit this one out.
Yes, friend. Verse 6 says the money is "…to buy timber and dressed stone to repair the temple." That's for the carpenters, builders and masons. Nobody ever fixed a wall with good intentions alone.

Silver is a fair guess since we're talking about money, but it isn't what they buy. Verse 6 says the money is "…to buy timber and dressed stone to repair the temple." Nobody ever patched a wall with a coin, friend.

That's the word, friend. King Josiah says they "…need not account for the money put into their hands, since they work with integrity." (2 Kings 22:7). That's a real compliment from the king himself. Being trusted like that is worth more than a whole tray of warm cookies.

Yes! Hilkiah says, "I have found the Book of the Law in the house of the LORD!" (2 Kings 22:8). He hands it to Shaphan, who reads it. It's like finding your keys in the pocket of the coat you wore yesterday, except this time it's the Book of the Law.

The ark of the covenant is a famous name, but it isn't what Hilkiah says he found. His words are, "I have found the Book of the Law in the house of the LORD!" (2 Kings 22:8). It's a book, and Shaphan reads it. Hold onto that, friend.

Moses made a bronze serpent (Numbers 21:9), but it's not in this verse. Hilkiah says, "I have found the Book of the Law in the house of the LORD!" (2 Kings 22:8). The thing he hands over to Shaphan is a book. Then Shaphan reads it.

This one is true, friend. In verse 13 Josiah says, "…great is the wrath of the LORD that burns against us because our fathers have not obeyed the words of this book…" The king names the fathers' disobedience to the book as the reason. It's a heavy thing to say out loud.

Yes, friend. Verse 14 says the men "…went and spoke to Huldah the prophetess…" She lived in Jerusalem, and she's the one who gives them the LORD's message (2 Kings 22:15). And hear this: the king's own men come to her door.

I can see why sorrow came to mind after all that heavy news. But the LORD tells Josiah, "…you will be gathered to your grave in peace." (2 Kings 22:20). The word is peace. It's a word of peace right after the hard news.

Not quite, friend. The LORD tells Josiah, "Your eyes will not see all the calamity that I will bring on this place." (2 Kings 22:20). So the card has it backwards. The text says Josiah's eyes will not see all of it.
